title: MFE Integration
text:
The BRDR alignment UI is available as reusable micro-frontends (MFE’s) so another application can embed the alignment flow without rebuilding the full demo host viewer.
Available MFE routes:

/alignment-mfe.html: GRB full workflow
/alignment-mfe-simple.html: GRB compact workflow
/alignment-mfe-wfs.html: BRK/WFS full workflow
/alignment-mfe-wfs-simple.html: BRK/WFS compact workflow

title: MFE Integration
text:
Integration Model
The current integration contract is based on an iframe plus postMessage. The recommended production setup is to use a sandboxed iframe, explicit target origins, and strict runtime validation of message payloads.
Flow:

Host application loads the MFE in an iframe.
MFE emits BRDR_ALIGNMENT_READY.
Host sends the selected geometry and CRS using BRDR_ALIGNMENT_INIT.
User works in the MFE and clicks Aanpassen.
MFE emits BRDR_ALIGNMENT_APPLY with the aligned geometry.

The same MFE can be embedded same-origin or cross-origin, provided the host validates both event.origin and event.source correctly, uses explicit targetOrigin values, and avoids mixed-content situations.

title: MFE Integration
MFE Integration
MFE Integration
text:
Same-Origin and Cross-Origin Notes

Same-origin embedding works directly.
Cross-origin embedding is supported in the MFE handshake.
Host and MFE should both reject messages from unexpected event.source windows.
Pass the expected host origin in the MFE URL, for example ?hostOrigin=https://host.example.com.
The MFE can optionally enforce an allowlist via VITE_BRDR_ALLOWED_HOST_ORIGINS.
If VITE_BRDR_ALLOWED_HOST_ORIGINS is not configured, the MFE stays non-blocking for demo deployments.
If the host runs on https, the MFE should also be served on https.
https host + http MFE will be blocked by browsers as mixed content.

title: Development and deployment commands
text:
Build and test
Build the viewers:
cd apps/brdr-viewers
npm ci
npm run build
Run the API tests:
cd services/brdr-api
..\..\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"
Build the single Docker image used by the current deployment flow:
docker build -f Dockerfile . -t brdr-webservice
Build the MapStore demo bundle:
cd mapstore/demo
npm run compile
npm run verify:demo

title: Development and deployment commands
text:
Local Docker demo
From the mapstore folder:
docker compose up --build
This starts the BRDR service on port 8000 and the MapStore demo on port 8081.

title: Development and deployment commands
text:
Azure helpers
The scripts in deploy/azure/ are optional PowerShell/CMD wrappers:

az-acr-build-push: build and push with Azure Container Registry Build.
az-acr-local-build-push: local Docker build and push.
az-deploy: deploy the configured single image to Web App or Container Apps.
az-aci-refresh-latest: recreate an existing ACI group with the latest image.

Copy deploy/azure/azure-deploy.settings.ps1.example to deploy/azure/azure-deploy.settings.ps1, fill in the Azure values, and run the desired wrapper from the repository root, for example:
.\deploy\azure\az-deploy.ps1 -Target webapp -SettingsFile .\deploy\azure\azure-deploy.settings.ps1

title: Run Locally
text:
Common Issues

Viewer shows fetch errors

Ensure backend is running on http://127.0.0.1:80.
Check CORS origin (localhost:5173 / 127.0.0.1:5173).
Verify outbound access from backend to GRB upstream services.



Empty or flat chart values

Trigger recalculation after drawing or editing geometry.
Ensure geometry is valid and has area.

title: Overview
text:
This project provides a proof-of-concept stack to align user geometries against GRB reference data:

a FastAPI webservice (services/brdr-api)
host viewers to draw/select geometries and launch BRDR alignment
reusable BRDR alignment micro-frontends (MFE’s) for embedding in another host application
Docker and local scripts for quick startup

title: Architecture
text:
A host viewer or embedded MFE works with a GeoJSON input geometry.
The backend loads the configured reference data and evaluates multiple distances.
The backend returns viewer-oriented BRDR output via /aligner.
The BRDR alignment MFE renders:

result geometry
result_diff_min (negative diff)
result_diff_plus (positive diff)
diffs chart values per distance step

In host-viewer mode, the selected geometry can be replaced with the aligned result.

title: Architecture
text:
Backend

Framework: FastAPI
Main file: services/brdr-api/brdr_webservice.py
Typings/models: services/brdr-api/brdr_webservice_typings.py
BRDR dependency: brdr package

Important behavior:

Request validation on feature IDs (must be present and unique).
Compatibility handling for GRB type labels across BRDR versions.
503 when upstream GRB service is unavailable.

title: Architecture
text:
Frontend Split
The frontend is intentionally split into two roles.

1. Host Viewers

Framework: React + TypeScript + Vite
Map library: OpenLayers
Routes:

/grb-viewer
/brk-viewer


Capabilities:

draw a new point/line/polygon
select a geometry from the map or list
import geometry as WKT / GeoJSON
export selected geometry as WKT / GeoJSON
open either the full or compact BRDR alignment MFE



2. BRDR Alignment MFE’s

Framework: React + TypeScript + Vite
Map library: OpenLayers
Routes:

/alignment-mfe.html
/alignment-mfe-simple.html
/alignment-mfe-wfs.html
/alignment-mfe-wfs-simple.html


Capabilities:

receive geometry and CRS from a host via postMessage
calculate BRDR output through /aligner
inspect prediction steps and aligned result
return the selected aligned geometry back to the host

Integration variants:

full: includes chart/timeline navigation
compact: optimized for faster prediction switching

title: API and Viewer
text:
Host Viewer Behaviour
The demo host viewers:

keeps an input geometry in local state
sends that geometry to /aligner
updates timeline and map layers from returned series and diffs
highlights prediction steps and can jump to previous/next prediction quickly
can replace the selected geometry with the aligned result
can import and export WKT / GeoJSON in multiple CRS variants

Main frontend files:

src/api/brdrApi.ts
src/state/useBrdrState.ts
src/components/map/MapView.tsx
src/components/demo/DemoMapViewer.tsx

For embedding details of the reusable BRDR alignment MFE’s, see MFE Integration.
